To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
apo-SOD1, A4V, G94R, and H40Q are partially unfolded in solution at 37 degrees C and that the unfolding of the proteins occurs non-cooperatively.
the apo-SOD1 proteins have a partially unfolded conformation at physiological temperature and that they unfold in a non-cooperative manner.

the structure and unfolding of apo-SOD1, and of three different pathogenic variants of human SOD1 (G93R, A4V, and H48O) that cause familial ALS, have been studied with hydrogen/deuterium-exchange and mass spectrometric techniques, and that these proteins have a partially unfolded β-barrel at physiological temperatures and unfold non-co-operatively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of protein folding, protein structure, and protein function in solution.
the structure and function of superoxide dismutases, which catalyze the conversion of the superoxide anion to hydrogen peroxide and oxygen.
the structure and dynamics of proteins in solution and their relationship to function and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure and folding/unfolding properties of human wild-type Sod1 and variants are similar.
the structure of apo-SOD1, as well as three pathogenic SOD1 variants, is partially unfolded at 37 degrees C, and that unfolding of these proteins is not cooperative.
the SOD1 protein is not in a fully folded state at physiological temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the apo-SOD1 variants studied here have a partially unfolded, non-native structure at 37 degrees C, and that the unfolding of this non-native structure is not a single cooperative process.
the SOD1 variants studied here are in a partially unfolded state, with a significant proportion of the beta-barrels being well protected from exchange.

apo SOD1 and variants are not fully folded in solution at physiological temperature and that the partially unfolded state of the protein is not the result of misfolding but a consequence of the inherent properties of the protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the partially unfolded beta-barrels of wild-type and variant SOD1 proteins at physiological temperatures are not necessarily a consequence of misfolding or aggregation, but may be a normal feature of these proteins in solution.
the SOD1 protein, whether it is wild type or a mutant, exists in a partially unfolded state at physiological temperatures and that the unfolding of the protein does not occur cooperatively.
the partially unfolded beta-barrels of apo-SOD1, A4V, G48Q, and G93R are very similar to each other and are not very different from that of the native protein.
